title: CELL-WAFER FOUNDRY: litho-light periodic oxide cell wafers bonded to U.S. foundry periphery under an open bitline-group bond spec
status_reason: No physics kill: bond physics remains testable and the 0-EUV path stands. After parity, global-line coupling, SA area, deck cost, D2W, contamination and royalty corrections, the step-change factors roughly halve: capex 7.6x -> 3.6x and $/GB 0.36x -> 0.62x DDR5 (1T1C-64), and the 1T1C break-even moves from 16 to 28 tiers. Most of what remains is tier density that any in-house 3D DRAM gets; the split's own share is ~1.5x capex and only while existing logic capacity absorbs the periphery. The merchant/open-interface leg has no buyer, seller or royalty and is demoted to optional. Two new must-pass device gates were added: bond-plane hydrogen and the oxide sub-WL driver. The concept lives as the bond and integration scale path of whichever portfolio cell passes.

revised_verdicts.possible: YES (unchanged). No physics is violated. New measured risks: bond-plane hydrogen into top-tier oxide channels and TFTs (needs ~1,400-3,500x barrier attenuation; one ALD Al2O3 layer has shown ~18x) and a bootstrapped n-only oxide sub-WL driver holding levels under Vt drift. Anisotropic warp is solved by D2W (0.14 um vs a 0.50 um budget at 2.0 um pitch).
revised_verdicts.profitable: STEP CHANGE IF IT WORKS: capital intensity and EUV. 3.6x less new memory-fab capex per GB/month ($61 -> $17.1; was 7.6x) and 0 EUV layers vs 5-7. $/GB 0.62x DDR5 ($0.92; was 0.36x); density 3.6x 1b (was 4.5x); bitline energy 1.4x. Gain-cell variant: 5.9x capex, 0.38x $/GB, 5.8x density. All conditional on a 64-tier portfolio cell. The split itself contributes only ~1.5x capex (with existing logic capacity), so most of the factor is inherited from the cell's tiers.
revised_verdicts.doable: PROVABLE WITH $1M: PARTLY. Standalone, $795k of experiments ($995k with founder pay) settles bond opens/bridges/overlay/voids, bond-plane hydrogen, the oxide sub-WL driver and group select, adhesion and contamination on 4- and 8-tier coupons bonded D2W at a fab-grade partner by M22. It cannot settle a 64-tier cell, the deck-driven cell-wafer cost or merchant economics. Within the portfolio seed (~$60k funded): NO unless a bonding partner contributes in kind.

revised_experiment: Warped 4-tier (lot 1) and 8-tier (lot 2) In2O3/IGZO coupons with mini-arrays, a 196:1 oxide group-select mux and a bootstrapped 1:8 oxide sub-WL driver with VNWL clamps. Bonded D2W (primary) at 2.0 and 1.5 um at a fab-grade partner; W2W only if the anisotropic warp half-difference is <=40 um. GO on 8 tiers at M22 requires: opens <=1e-5/link over >=1e7 links and bridges <=1e-7 over >=3e7 pairs, both on CSAM-void-free fields; overlay <=0.30 um; >=95% void-free; ΔVt <=20 mV and retention change <=2x on top-tier cells AND selector/driver TFTs after bond, 3x260 C reflow and 1,000 h at 125 C, with D-labelled bond-surface ToF-SIMS showing no bond-origin hydrogen in the channel (barrier split none/Al2O3/Al2O3+SiN+Al2O3; anneal 150-300 C); WL driver level loss <=50 mV, edges <=10 ns, clamp <=-0.5 V after stress; tier-stack 4-point-bend Gc >=5 J/m2 with FIB on every failed chain; VPD-ICPMS <=1e10 at/cm2; Kelvin stable after 1,000 cycles (nanotwinned-Cu split); RTN/VRT of top vs bottom tiers at ns-us (select/read) and s (retention) timescales. Also: field-solver alpha and a <=4 um2, <=7 mV-sigma 28 nm SA on the MARGIN STACK MPW share, reading the oxide mux through the bonds. Cost: $740k + $55k contingency = $795k experiments (+$200k founder pay = $995k), M1-M24.

responses.response: Valid. Calling the predecode 'digital and offset-tolerant' was wrong: the n-only oxide TFT is an analog switch in the WL path, and an off pass gate leaves the WL floating. Redesign: a 1980s-style self-bootstrapped n-only sub-WL driver. The pass-TFT gate is precharged and then coupled up by the FX edge to ~3.0 + 0.7 x 3.0 = 5.1 V. That leaves 1.3 V of overdrive at VPP with an end-of-life Vt of 0.8 V. The WL high is therefore the silicon FX-rail level, and a 0.1 V PBTI drift changes R_on by ~8% (edge time), not the restore level. Each WL gets an active n-TFT clamp to the silicon VNWL rail (<=-0.5 V), so unselected WLs are held, not floating. VPP keeps >=150 mV of overdrive above the cell Vt, so the restore level is set by the bitline. Load per tier WL is 5,000 cells x 0.04 fF + wire = 260 fF. A 5 ns edge needs 156 uA, i.e. W ~0.8 um of short-channel ALD In2O3. Area is 7.4e6 WL segments x 0.45 um2 = 3.3 mm2 = 19% of the array. It does NOT fit the 8% edge budget the critic asked about, so it moves to a dedicated TFT driver plane over the array (+$60 per cell wafer). This is not demonstrated: it becomes a measured gate.
responses.action: Adopt the bootstrapped sub-WL driver with VNWL clamp on a dedicated TFT plane (+$60/cell wafer in cell_common_adders). Put it on coupon lot 1 driving a 260 fF dummy WL. Add kill K3b: <=50 mV level loss, <=10 ns edges and a <=-0.5 V clamp after 1,000 h at 125 C, else the TFT-predecode leg dies (revival: a layer-transferred thin-Si driver plane).

responses.response: Valid on both counts. (1) Parity: the 26 mV threshold requires BCH t=8 parity (15.6%). The model now uses ecc 1.156 for 1T1C, which alone takes density 2.01 -> 1.85 Gb/mm2 (-8%). (2) Coupling: modelled from geometry as 0.05 fF/um per side of the global line (~2/3 of 0.15 fF/um), giving alpha = 0.145 unshielded on the revised 73 um line, inside CIRC's 0.1-0.2. That needs S = 36.6 mV, Cs 2.05 fF and 1.43 Gb/mm2 (3.2x). Redesign: route global lines on two metal levels with a grounded shield between neighbours (+~$120/cell wafer). Residual alpha is 0.035, S 28.0 mV. Net CIRC-02 effect at the original SA size: 2.01 -> 1.81 Gb/mm2 (4.5x -> 4.0x, -10%) and $/GB 0.54 -> 0.60 (+11%). This meets the critic's '>=4x' condition only at a 2.5 um2 SA; with CIRC-03 the total is 3.6x. For comparison, the conventional 50 mV / 6.25% option with shielding gives 1.27 Gb/mm2 (2.8x). I-12302 plate-strip sensing (~135 mV vs ~14 mV) was considered. In this bond-group architecture it needs a local gain FET per 8-64-cell strip, which turns the 1T1C into the non-destructive spec class (equal to the gain-cell route: 2.60 Gb/mm2). It also faces Micron's planar prior art (US 5,991,216; 8,009,460), so it is kept as the 1T1C revival path, not the base.
responses.action: Model: ecc 1.0625 -> 1.156; c_cpl 0 -> 0.05 fF/um; shield_factor 0.25 with two shielded metal levels (+$120/cell wafer). This lowers the 1T1C density claim by ~10% (4.5x -> 4.0x before CIRC-03). Add field-solver alpha extraction to the experiment and a K5' re-scope trigger if shielded alpha >0.05.

responses.response: Valid: the base sat at the optimistic end. A 28 nm offset-cancelled SA with ECC-grade ~7 mV sigma, a write driver and restore through an oxide group select is taken as 4.0 um2 (was 2.5). M rises 146 -> 196, Cbl 19.9 -> 25.8 fF and Cs 1.22 -> 1.62 fF. Density goes 1.81 -> 1.60 Gb/mm2 (-12%) and $/GB +13% (0.60 -> 0.68 W2W). At 5 um2 it is 1.50 Gb/mm2 (3.4x). Restore through a 100 kOhm oxide select: tau = 100 kOhm x 25.8 fF = 2.6 ns, so 5 tau = 13 ns against a ~32 ns tRAS. Feasible, but it sets tRAS; a 2x-wide selector halves it. Side benefit: with the larger SA the group is SA-limited up to 2.0 um, so the spec pitch relaxes to 2.0 um at no density cost (overlay budget 0.375 -> 0.50 um). Gain cells absorb the larger SA with a bigger cluster (M 205 -> 328) and keep 2.60 Gb/mm2.
responses.action: Model: a_sa_um2 2.5 -> 4.0 (1T1C density -12%, to 3.6x 1b). Lay out the 28 nm SA with offset cancellation and write driver, with Monte Carlo, on the MARGIN STACK MPW share (target <=4 um2, sigma <=7 mV). Spec pitch 1.5 -> 2.0 um.

responses.response: Valid. The lumped-Cbl emulator measured only what the model had already shown to be negligible (bond parasitics are 2% of Cbl). It left out the oxide group select (kickback, Vt spread, R_on) and the oxide WL driver, which are the electrical novelties of the split. Fix: build a 196:1 oxide group-select mux and the bootstrapped 1:8 sub-WL driver on coupon lots 1 and 2. Characterise them pre-bond by probe. In lot 2, read them through the bonds with the MPW SA board: charge injection, R_on distribution, Vt spread, signal versus programmed Cbl. Incremental cost ~$10k in masks and test (lines B and E). This gives the raise a measured electrical chain from cell to oxide select to bond to SA.
responses.action: Add oxide group-select and sub-WL-driver test structures to both coupon lots, read through the bonds by the MPW board before the raise. K5' now counts oxide-select effects in the 5% sense-margin trigger.

responses.response: Valid and not refutable by arithmetic. 20 mV at EOT 3 nm allows 1.44e11 donors/cm2, i.e. 0.03-0.07% of the 2-5e14 H2O/cm2 bond-plane inventory. Molecular H2 diffuses ~137 um in SiO2 during a 250 C / 2 h anneal and ~2.9 mm over 10 yr at 85 C [UNVERIFIED-training D], so an oxide standoff does not help; only barriers do. If all of the inventory were mobile, the barrier stack must attenuate ~1,400-3,500x. A single O3-ALD Al2O3 barrier cut an IGZO TFT's hydrogen-exposure shift from ~-12 V to ~-0.66 V (~18x; Ajou, logged). A 3-layer Al2O3 / low-H SiN / Al2O3 stack is ~300-5,800x only if the layers act independently [SPECULATIVE]. Note that the split's 'hydrogen freedom' argument is now neutral: monolithic CuA has the periphery-BEOL hydrogen problem instead. I-12627 (series write devices square the leakage tail) does not rescue this, because bond-plane hydrogen is a correlated sheet source. Mitigation: barrier stack plus SiCN (lower OH than SiO2) bond dielectric, plus a measured gate. The gate uses D-labelled bond surfaces (D2O rinse or D-plasma), so ToF-SIMS separates bond-origin hydrogen from background. ΔVt is measured on top-tier cells AND selector/driver TFTs after the bond, 3 x 260 C reflow and 1,000 h at 125 C, across the barrier splits.
responses.action: Add an Al2O3/low-H SiN/Al2O3 barrier under the bond layer (+$20/cell wafer). Add the D-labelled ToF-SIMS + 1,000 h 125 C + reflow gate and the barrier split to lot 1 (FA line F +$35k). Extend K3' to cover selector/driver TFTs and the best barrier. Revival if it fails: Cu-only room-temperature SAB, or TFTs on the substrate side.

responses.response: Valid. The single-Ea map (250 C x 2 h = 0.09-0.36 yr at 85 C) assumes one process. At bond temperatures, hydrogen release from SiCN/SiN, transport through barriers and oxygen exchange in IGZO switch on, and none of them runs at 85 C. The map is therefore at best a lower bound and is withdrawn as the basis for the <=250 C spec. The model now prints that caveat. The anneal temperature is set empirically: ΔVt versus anneal at 150/200/250/300 C, plus a 3 x 260 C reflow profile, on coupons. Only if one activation energy fits both the anneal series and 85 C aging is the Arrhenius extrapolation used for lifetime.
responses.action: Model s5 carries a RED-TEAM CAVEAT that the Arrhenius map is a lower bound. Add a 150 C point to the anneal split (was 200/250/300) and a reflow profile. The spec temperature becomes provisional until GATE 1.

responses.response: Valid on the premises: an un-bootstrapped n-only pass gate loses a Vt, and PBTI drift would come off the WL high. The micro-second speed of display gate drivers comes from pF panel loads and um-long channels, not from bootstrapping. Here the load is ~260 fF, so W ~0.8 um of short-channel ALD In2O3 at ~200 uA/um [UNVERIFIED-training drive] gives a 5 ns edge. With a bootstrapped gate (~5.1 V) and a silicon-defined FX level, the 50-100 mV drift appears as an ~8% R_on change, not a level loss. Without >=1:8 predecode, WL bonds exceed sites at 1.5-2.0 um, so this leg is necessary. The critic's would-change-my-mind test (1:8 IGZO predecode, 3.0 V WL, <=10 ns edges, <=50 mV loss after 1,000 h at 125 C) is adopted verbatim as a gate.
responses.action: Same redesign as CIRC-01 (bootstrapped SWD + VNWL clamp, dedicated TFT plane). Adopt DEV's test as K3b at M14, with stress running in parallel with the lot 1 bake.

responses.response: Valid. ALD laminates (Al2O3/HfO2/TiN/IGZO) can have Gc of a few J/m2. Thinning, the 17 vs ~0.5 ppm/K Cu/SiO2 CTE mismatch and thermal cycling load the weakest plane, and delamination inside the stack would read as bond opens. Fix: four-point-bend Gc on the tier-stack laminates (target >=5 J/m2). Add unbonded control daisy chains through the tiers that see the same thinning and cycling, so stack failures are separated from bond failures. FIB every failed chain (~25 lamellae, was 15). A delamination inside the stack is a cell-stack problem; it would also hit monolithic CuA. It is routed to the cell's owner and not counted against the bond.
responses.action: Add four-point bend (~$12k), unbonded control chains and FIB-every-failure to line F. Add GO item tier-stack Gc >=5 J/m2. The failure-attribution rule is in revised §9.

responses.response: Valid as a value-capture objection. The generic split is anticipated and already runs in-house, and a royalty-free spec earns nothing. The supply-adjacency claim is also avoidable: a designer can cluster supply pads instead of domain-switching them. The mission does not kill on business grounds, and this changes no physics or step-change number. It does change the plan. The spec is published as a defensive, reciprocal-licence standard, not a revenue engine. Value is captured through: (a) implementation claims on the bond-ready oxide cell wafer (stress-compensated, hydrogen-barriered, co-specified with a measured anneal/reflow budget); (b) the bootstrapped oxide sub-WL driver plane with VNWL clamps; (c) D-labelled bond-hydrogen qualification and bond-link BIST/remap methods; (d) bundling with whichever portfolio cell passes. Standards spending is cut from $20k to $5k until an adopter appears.
responses.action: Re-base the IP strategy: defensive open spec with reciprocal licence; provisionals on the bond-ready oxide stack, the oxide SWD plane and the D-labelled qualification method. Drop the claim that the adjacency rule is unavoidable. Budget line I $20k -> $5k.

responses.response: Valid, and worse after the red-team corrections. The revised capex factor is 3.6x (1T1C-64), of which 3.3x is good GB per wafer (tier density) that any in-house 3D DRAM also gets. A monolithic in-house 3D DRAM that must process its own periphery needs ~$26.4 per GB/month against $17.1 for the split, so the split's own share is ~1.5x, and only while existing 28 nm logic capacity absorbs the periphery (1.0x if it must be built). The null-hypothesis bar rises: the W2W premium is $977/pair, needing >=$15.3/tier at 64 tiers (51% of a $30 tier). D2W costs $1,369 net of a $208 KGD saving, needing >=$21.4/tier, because a cell-only wafer cannot be fully KGD-tested (owner correction: 50% screen capture). Partial counter-evidence: Samsung chose W2W peri-under-cell bonding for its IGZO 4F2 VCT, and Kioxia/YMTC bond NAND. Incumbents with both options pick the bond, but that supports the in-house split, not the merchant one. No data shows a $15/tier NAND-line advantage.
responses.action: Restate the step-change claim as inherited: 3.6x capex / 0.62x $/GB comes mostly from the cell's tiers, and the split adds ~1.5x conditional. D1' threshold raised to $15.3 (W2W) / $21.4 (D2W) per tier. Commission a per-tier fab-cost comparison (NAND line vs logic BEOL) as a raise-stage item.

responses.response: Valid. No merchant cell-wafer seller or buyer exists. Every plausible cell-wafer maker is vertically integrated, no U.S. NAND-class line exists, and an owned line exceeds a $10-50M round. Per the mission this is not a kill, since a market structure is not physics, and logic had no merchant foundry before 1987. But the 'merchant' adjective and the U.S.-supply-independence step change cannot be claimed today. The first realistic adopter is in-house: a U.S. memory maker (Micron) bonding its own oxide cell wafers to U.S. logic periphery, or a NAND maker with idle decks using the spec internally. The U.S.-manufacturability claim is downgraded from 'step change' to 'enabler'. The periphery is U.S.-sourceable on existing logic capacity, and the cell line needs a partner.
responses.action: Demote the merchant leg to optional. Retarget scale-path partners to in-house adopters (Micron + U.S. logic periphery; a NAND maker with idle decks). Revival of the merchant leg: an LOI from a cell-wafer maker plus a periphery foundry agreeing to trade wafers under the spec.

responses.response: Valid. Inside the portfolio seed only ~$60k (spec, IP, standards) is funded, so the seed alone tests no bond physics. Standalone, university-cleanroom particles could trip K4: W2W void yield is 0.67 at 0.5/cm2 and 0.20 at 2/cm2 in the revised model. Fixes: (1) all bond-layer CMP, clean, inspection and bonding at a fab-grade partner, with particle maps logged per wafer; (2) opens/bridges counted only on CSAM-void-free fields, so particle density cannot masquerade as bond physics; (3) D2W primary, which confines voids to one die (void yield 0.905 even at 0.5/cm2, $1.00/GB vs $1.30 W2W); (4) pursue in-kind bonding through a NY CREATES/NSTC startup programme or a bonder-vendor demo lab. Honest verdict: provable within the portfolio seed = No unless that in-kind partner commits; standalone = Partly at $795k of experiments.
responses.action: Make the fab-grade partner a Q1 gate (quote <=$275k or in-kind commitment, else switch partner). Adopt void-free-field accounting in GO/K2'/K4'. State the portfolio-seed provability as No in §0/§11.

responses.response: Valid; now quantified, with honest uncertainty. Adeia terms are confidential, so the model books 1% of pair cost: $77/pair on the revised $7.7k pair, +~$0.01/GB (~1%). That is at the critic's <1% threshold but cannot be verified. The royalty also widens the split's premium over monolithic CuA by ~$1.2/tier at 64 tiers. The original Ziptronix DBI families were filed around 2000-2005 and expire before a ~2030 product [UNVERIFIED-training], so the exposure is to later improvement patents. R&D bonding at a licensed partner remains low-risk.
responses.action: Model: dbi_royalty_frac 0 -> 0.01 (included in the pair cost and the null-hypothesis premium). FTO: claims review of the post-2010 Adeia families before the raise. Bond via a licensed partner.

responses.response: Valid. Using the model's own Delta = b*t/r, a +300/-550 um saddle gives +1.55 / -2.84 um run-out. Isotropic correction removes only the -0.65 um mean, leaving +/-2.20 um, 5.9x the 0.375 um budget at 1.5 um. W2W needs an anisotropic half-difference <=73 um with perfect isotropic correction (PROC's ~40 um gate adopted). Redesign: D2W becomes the primary bond mode. Each ~4 mm die is flattened alone, so the worst wafer curvature (0.049/m) gives only 0.038 um of die-level run-out. Adding 0.10 um (3 sigma) placement (Besi CHAMEO ultra plus AC, logged) gives 0.14 um, a 2.7x margin at 1.5 um. The spec pitch also moves to 2.0 um at no density cost (the SA-limited group), giving a 0.50 um budget, 3.6x margin and a 97 um W2W saddle allowance. D2W is priced by throughput at +$600/pair with partial cell-die screening, so $/GB is $0.92 D2W vs $0.91 W2W: cost-neutral. Stress-balanced 0/90 deg die orientation is kept as a W2W revival lever.
responses.action: D2W primary; spec pitch 2.0 um (1.5 alternate, 1.0 dropped). Both-axis shape maps and IR verniers. K1' drops W2W (not the concept) if the anisotropic half-difference stays >40 um. Model: d2w_extra_cost 300 -> 600, cell_kgd_capture 1.0 -> 0.5, plus an anisotropic warp section.

responses.response: Valid. Per-cell isolation at 40 nm CD through ~4.5 um is AR ~112, beyond the ~50-70 production limit. The original $700 + $30/tier contained no HAR-module or staircase cost at all. Revised model: decks limited to AR 60 (2.4 um, ~34 tiers), so 64 tiers need 2 decks (128 need 4), at $800 per deck for the HAR modules, staircase and inter-deck plug. With +$200 of adders the 64-tier cell wafer rises $2,620 -> $4,420 (1.7x) and the pair $5,820 -> $7,797. 1T1C $/GB goes 0.68 -> 0.87 at this step (0.91 W2W / 0.92 D2W all-in), and cost break-even moves 16 -> 28 tiers. PROC's 2x case ($1,300/deck, ~$5.4k cell wafer) gives $1.03/GB. 128 tiers no longer beats 64 for 1T1C (the minimum is ~$0.87 at ~96 tiers), because decks scale with tiers. A self-isolating channel-last flow (ALD channel only in lateral recesses around each VBL) could avoid the slit, but it is unproven and not credited.
responses.action: Model: deck_cost 0 -> $800 with n_decks = ceil(tiers x 70 nm / (40 nm x 60)). This lowers the $/GB step from 0.36x to 0.62x DDR5 (together with the other corrections; decks alone add +$0.19/GB) and raises the 1T1C break-even to 28 tiers. Ask a 3D-DRAM integrator for a <=2-deck 64-tier flow as a raise-stage diligence item.

responses.response: Valid for the merchant model: In and Ga are acceptors in Si and Zn is a deep level, so logic foundries keep them off shared CMP/bond tools. Mitigation: (1) the cell wafer presents only Cu/SiCN at its bond face, because the oxide semiconductors are buried under the redistribution BEOL and the Al2O3/SiN barrier. Bevel and backside are encapsulated, and an edge-trim/bevel clean is done before shipping. (2) The open spec gains a contamination clause: VPD-ICPMS <=1e10 at/cm2 In/Ga/Zn on front, bevel and backside before entering a bond line, the same route foundries already use to admit eMRAM/FeRAM materials into BEOL. (3) D2W bonding runs in a packaging-class line used to non-Si materials. Bond cost is raised $400 -> $500/pair for a segregated or qualified line (+$0.01/GB). Partial rebuttal: 'CuA avoids the problem entirely' holds only for in-house memory fabs. Monolithic CuA at a logic foundry puts In/Ga/Zn into the foundry's own BEOL tools, which is worse than receiving an encapsulated wafer.
responses.action: Model: bond_cost_pair 400 -> 500. Add a VPD-ICPMS qualification of coupon wafers before bonding (line F). Add the contamination clause and encapsulation requirement to spec v0.1. The bonding-partner gate requires acceptance of oxide-semiconductor wafers.

responses.response: Valid. Low-temperature Cu/SiCN bonding gives up Cu interdiffusion and pad reliability unless the Cu microstructure is engineered. Interface water sits directly above the top tiers, and 3 x ~260 C reflows add thermal dose after the test. Fixes: (1) a nanotwinned (111) Cu split for <=200-250 C bonding; (2) Kelvin-resistance stability after 1,000 thermal cycles (was 500); (3) 3 x 260 C reflow is added before the post-bond ΔVt/retention and ToF-SIMS measurements; (4) the interface-water term is handled by the DEV-01 barrier and D-labelled hydrogen gate. A 260 C reflow drives H2 ~29 um in SiO2 [UNVERIFIED-training D], so it is a hydrogen-transport event, not just added dose.
responses.action: Add the nanotwinned-Cu split, 1,000-cycle Kelvin stability and 3 x 260 C reflow to the GO list and to K3'. The PROC test (ToF-SIMS after bond + 3 x reflow, dVt <=20 mV, Kelvin stable after 1,000 cycles) is adopted as written.
